title: Choose the DOM X-Ray visual world
question: Which physical metaphor should govern the first interactive result viewer? Keep one, steer the hand, or re-roll.

options.label: Survey Bench
options.lineage: cartographic relief maps and measured survey tables
options.thesis: The captured page becomes a measured relief whose elevation is DOM ancestry, never performance or importance.
options.viewport: A full-width measured relief dominates the screen; a cross-section rail cuts through it while the hero fact and URL sit as quiet field notes at the margins.
options.risk: Elevation could be mistaken for quality; every view must label it as DOM depth and keep the formula one action away.

raised.raise: The section rail now steps on a fixed numbered graticule with keyboard-addressable measurement cursors.
The measured world owns the whole viewport instead of being trapped inside a dashboard card.
Active tools receive unmistakable physical stamp states instead of generic selected pills.
Structure, weight, and origins each change material behavior—not merely accent color.

options.label: Architectural Section Table
options.lineage: architectural museum models and the approved DOM X-Ray atlas
options.thesis: A familiar webpage peels into a physical cutaway whose plates, mass, and external machinery remain tied to inspectable evidence.
options.viewport: The page stands nearly front-on on a warm inspection table, then its measured layers separate in depth; one precise fact and one URL action anchor the left edge.
options.risk: It is the most familiar direction from the approved atlas, so execution must go beyond a tasteful 3D stack and make evidence inspection unforgettable.

options.label: Celestial Dependency Atlas
options.lineage: celestial star charts and coordinate plates
options.thesis: Page regions become chart plates while resource mass sets magnitude and third-party origins form named constellations beyond the viewport boundary.
options.viewport: A dark coordinate field fills the screen with the recognizable page as a bright chart plate; exact resources orbit as magnitude-ranked marks with sparse marginal readouts.
options.case: It strongly identifies with technical early adopters and could produce striking shares, but makes DOM geometry less immediately literal than the survey bench.
options.risk: Constellations can imply relationships the scan did not measure; only exact resource links may connect, and decorative mythic figures are omitted.

options.label: Multiplane Page Stage
options.lineage: multiplane cel-animation cameras and painted stage flats
options.thesis: The visible page is one composed image until the camera racks focus and separates its measured structural planes.
options.viewport: The page fills the center as a crisp front cel; the reveal pulls through layered planes while evidence labels remain fixed on the nearest clear acetate.
options.case: Its native motion explains depth beautifully and holds product clarity, but its cinematic softness weakens the serious-instrument character.
options.risk: Painted atmosphere could overpower truth; all page geometry must stay diagrammatic and screenshot-derived rather than illustrative.

options.label: Oscilloscope Signal Bench
options.thesis: The page becomes a triggered measurement trace with resource channels and movable cursors.
options.viewport: One ten-division screen overlays structure and transfer channels with numeric readouts below.
options.case: Developers recognize the instrument, but a continuous waveform falsely suggests time-series evidence the first version does not capture.
options.kept: A fixed measurement grid and cursor controls with discrete, reproducible steps.
options.risk: It would push the product toward dark technical nostalgia and away from a public, spatial page cutaway.

options.label: Experiential Shader Portal
options.thesis: The scan result fills the browser as one living GPU field with marginal evidence controls.
options.viewport: A fullscreen reactive field carries the scene while thin labels sit at the outer edges.
options.case: It identifies with creative technologists, but the shader becomes the subject and obscures the measured page.
options.kept: Total first-viewport commitment: the artifact fills the screen and the interface recedes.
options.risk: It drifts toward decorative WebGL, exactly the category DOM X-Ray must refuse.

options.label: Earthy Identity System
options.thesis: A warm stamped field manual turns scans into friendly mapped stations.
options.viewport: A world-map sheet organizes the scan as tactile stations with stamped completion states.
options.case: The tone is humane, but neither the audience nor the mechanism naturally belongs to lifestyle packaging.
options.kept: Controls should feel physically marked and unmistakably active, not cosmetically highlighted.
options.risk: It could make a precise browser measurement feel folksy and commercially nostalgic.

options.label: Measured Material Shelf
options.thesis: Each exploration mode matures as a distinct vessel with visible material state.
options.viewport: Three state vessels sit on a measured shelf with dated labels and thresholds.
options.case: The material states are legible, but the culinary ritual has no credible relationship to page structure or transfer evidence.
options.kept: Modes must differ through material behavior and interaction, not just color tinting.
options.risk: The metaphor would become whimsical decoration and could imply change over time that was not recorded.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished dark developer dashboard places a Three.js model beside metric cards and familiar filters.
canonCard.viewport: A top bar and left control rail frame a centered 3D page model with KPI cards on the right.
canonCard.risk: Immediately usable but interchangeable with existing observability products, and 3D reads as decoration.
